facts.statement: Partial remains of Asylosaurus were discovered in the autumn of 1834 and initially described in 1836 by Henry Riley and Samuel Stutchbury as belonging to Thecodontosaurus.
facts.quote: It is based on partial remains, discovered in the autumn of 1834, described in 1836 by Henry Riley and Samuel Stutchbury as pertaining to Thecodontosaurus

facts.statement: The remains were brought to Yale University by Othniel Charles Marsh between 1888 and 1890, allowing them to survive a 1940 World War II bombardment that destroyed the original holotype of Thecodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh brought to Yale University between 1888 and 1890. These remains thus escaped destruction by a bombardment in 1940 during World War II, unlike the original holotype of Thecodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Asylosaurus was formally described as a distinct genus in 2007 by Peter Galton.
facts.quote: Asylosaurus was described in 2007 by Peter Galton.

facts.statement: The type species is named A. yalensis, which refers to Yale University.
facts.quote: The type species is A. yalensis, referring to Yale.

facts.statement: The fossils originated from a Rhaetian-age cave fill at Durdham Down in Clifton, Bristol.
facts.quote: The bones originally came from a Rhaetian-age cave fill at Durdham Down, Clifton, Bristol.

facts.statement: The genus is based on specimen YPM 2195, a partial skeleton containing the torso, back vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, shoulder girdle, humeri, forearm, and hand.
facts.quote: Asylosaurus is based on YPM 2195, a partial skeleton of the torso region, including back vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, a shoulder girdle, humeri, a partial forearm, and a hand

facts.statement: Asylosaurus differs from similar contemporaneous basal sauropodomorphs like Thecodontosaurus and Pantydraco in the structure of its humerus.
facts.quote: It differs from Thecodontosaurus and Pantydraco, contemporaneous basal sauropodomorphs of similar builds, in the structure of its humerus (upper arm).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Asylosaurus may have occupied a separate ecological niche from related animals based on whether it was omnivorous or herbivorous.
facts.quote: It may have had a separate ecological niche from these other related animals based on how omnivorous or herbivorous it was.

facts.statement: According to Gregory S. Paul, Asylosaurus measured 2 meters in length and weighed approximately 250 kilograms.
facts.quote: According to Gregory S. Paul, it was 2 m long and its weight was about 250 kg.

facts.statement: Asylosaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropodomorpha.
Asylosaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
Asylosaurus lived during the Rhaetian stage, between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Asylosaurus is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic of England.
rejected.quote: Asylosaurus (meaning "unharmed or sanctuary lizard") is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic Avon Fissure Fill of England.
